Identified Set for Population Size under Detection Feedback

Source: R/feedback_sensitivity.R
feedback_identified_set.Rd

Bounds the population size over a range of \(\delta\), with a confidence interval for the true value or for the whole set.

Usage

feedback_identified_set(
  x,
  delta_range = NULL,
  level = 0.95,
  method = c("imbens_manski", "union"),
  se = c("sd", "iqr")
)

# S3 method for class 'uncounted_feedback_set'
print(x, ...)

Arguments

x

An "uncounted_feedback" object.

delta_range

Length-2 range of \(\delta\). Defaults to x$admissible_range.

level

Confidence level.

method

"imbens_manski" covers the true \(\xi_g\) (Imbens and Manski, 2004). "union" covers the whole set, so it is wider.

se

How to measure the spread of the replicate bounds on the log scale: "sd", or "iqr" for \(\mathrm{IQR} / 1.349\).

...

Ignored.

Value

A data frame of class "uncounted_feedback_set" with one row per group and columns group, L, U, delta_at_min, delta_at_max, ci_lower, ci_upper, c, Delta, se_L and se_U. Without a bootstrap in x the interval columns are NA.

Details

With \(D\) = delta_range, the bounds are \(L_g = \min_{\delta \in D} \xi_g(\delta)\) and \(U_g = \max_{\delta \in D} \xi_g(\delta)\). They are found on a grid and refined with optimize(), not read from the ends of \(D\), because group totals need not be monotone in \(\delta\). Replicate bounds are replicate-wise minima and maxima over \(D\).

"imbens_manski", on the log scale with \(\Delta = \log U_g - \log L_g\), solves for \(c\) in $$\Phi\left(c + \frac{\Delta}{\max(s_L, s_U)}\right) - \Phi(-c) = \mathrm{level},$$ which lies between qnorm(level) and qnorm((1 + level) / 2), and returns \(\exp(\log L_g - c s_L)\) and \(\exp(\log U_g + c s_U)\). "union" returns the \((1 - \mathrm{level}) / 2\) quantile of the replicate \(L_g\) and the \((1 + \mathrm{level}) / 2\) quantile of the replicate \(U_g\).

Validity. The Imbens–Manski interval requires superefficient estimation of \(\Delta\) (Stoye, 2009). Stoye's Lemma 3 gives this when the bounds are jointly asymptotically normal and \(U_g \ge L_g\) by construction, as here. Normality can fail when the minimum or maximum over \(D\) is attained at more than one \(\delta\), so treat the intervals with caution if delta_at_min or delta_at_max is interior to \(D\). \(D\) itself is treated as fixed.

References

Imbens, G. W. and Manski, C. F. (2004). Confidence intervals for partially identified parameters. Econometrica, 72(6), 1845–1857. doi:10.1111/j.1468-0262.2004.00555.x

Stoye, J. (2009). More on confidence intervals for partially identified parameters. Econometrica, 77(4), 1299–1315. doi:10.3982/ECTA7347
